independent_reference.source: Hand-derivation in tools/testkit/golden/derivations/physarum-deposit-step1.md §§ 1-3. With a zero initial trail, the sense step returns identical zero readings at all three offsets; the rotate step is a tie at every agent; the canonical deterministic tie-breaker keeps the current heading. Each agent then moves +1 along its cardinal heading and writes the deposit constant (5.0) to the destination cell. Four deposits land at exact integer cells (5, 4), (10, 4), (4, 12), (11, 10); the total mass before the diffuse+decay step is 4 * 5.0 = 20.0; the multiplicative decay (1 - 0.1) then yields a post-decay total mass of 18.0. All steps shown by hand.

independent_reference.source: Jones, J. (2010), 'Characteristics of pattern formation and evolution in approximations of Physarum transport networks', Artificial Life 16 (2), 127-153. DOI 10.1162/artl.2010.16.2.16202. § 3 (Table 1) fixes the canonical parameter set (delta_phi = 45 deg, L_sense = 9, L_move = 1, deposit = 5.0, decay_alpha = 0.1) and § 3 prose fixes the five-component step order (sense -> rotate -> move -> deposit -> diffuse+decay). Applied to the zero-trail 4-agent fixture above, Jones-2010's update rule is closed-form: every sense read is zero (no trail); every rotate is a tie (no preference); every move advances one cell along the cardinal heading; every deposit writes 5.0 at the destination; total mass after diffuse (mass-preserving) + decay = 20.0 * (1 - 0.1) = 18.0.
